claims.claim_text: The TruFor image-level manipulation score is 1.000.
claims.brief_justification: Reported detector score; not checkable against the supplied imagery.

The annotated giraffe is only ~90x150 px in a wide, soft shot; tight crops of the same area in A and B look closely similar (profile stance, neck raised to the right, head pointing right), so neither a difference nor an absence of difference can be established reliably. A maximal score also cannot itself demonstrate 'no manipulation'.

claims.claim_text: There is a localized region in the bottom-center.
claims.brief_justification: IMAGE C's white giraffe-shaped silhouette sits in the bottom-centre cell (only its head tip touches the centre cell); IMAGE D's outline is in the same place.

claims.claim_text: That region has a high probability score.
claims.brief_justification: Reported numeric detector output, not verifiable from imagery.

claims.claim_text: This suggests the presence of a real object in the image.
claims.brief_justification: A giraffe is indeed visible at the annotated location, but the inference that its presence is therefore unaltered is not established by the supplied evidence at this resolution.

notes: Location matches the annotation. The explanation's internal logic is inconsistent (a score of 1.000 read as 'no manipulation' while the annotation marks a region of interest), but the annotated giraffe is too small and soft in both A and B for me to judge whether its content differs, so the manipulation judgement is left uncertain.
